The ultrasound data have three layers: participants, visits within participants (day-to-day variation) and images within visits (measurement error). The matching model is

```r
lmer(VL_CSA_cm2 ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID/Week_f), data = img)
# (1 | ID/Week_f) = (1 | ID) + (1 | ID:Week_f)
```

Averaging the images first gives the same answer when every visit has the same number of images and there are no image-level predictors. Leaving out the visit level, i.e. `(1 | ID)` on image rows, is pseudoreplication at the visit level.

## Explore: power calculator

Simulate trials like this one (3 visits, random intercept) and estimate the power to detect a given difference in change at week 12. Defaults use the variance components from the course data. Each run fits `nsim` mixed models in your browser (about 0.25 s each), so press **Run Code** when you've set the sliders.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof pw_n     = Inputs.range([6, 60], {value: 20, step: 1, label: "Participants per arm"})
viewof pw_delta = Inputs.range([0, 2], {value: 0.6, step: 0.05, label: "True difference in change (cm²)"})
viewof pw_sdres = Inputs.range([0.2, 1.2], {value: 0.61, step: 0.01, label: "Within-person residual SD"})
viewof pw_drop  = Inputs.range([0, 0.3], {value: 0.1, step: 0.01, label: "Dropout before week 12"})
viewof pw_nsim  = Inputs.range([50, 400], {value: 100, step: 50, label: "Simulations"})
```

```{webr}
#| input:
#|   - pw_n
#|   - pw_delta
#|   - pw_sdres
#|   - pw_drop
#|   - pw_nsim
#| caption: Power by simulation
sim_trial <- function(n, delta, sd_id = 2.94, sd_res = 0.61, drop = 0) {
  ids <- factor(seq_len(2 * n))
  d <- expand.grid(ID = ids, Week = c(0, 6, 12))
  d$Group <- factor(ifelse(as.integer(d$ID) <= n, "Placebo", "Protein"),
                    levels = c("Placebo", "Protein"))
  u <- rnorm(2 * n, 0, sd_id)
  d$y <- 25 + u[d$ID] + 1.05 * d$Week / 12 +
    delta * (d$Week / 12) * (d$Group == "Protein") + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, sd_res)
  gone <- ids[runif(2 * n) < drop]
  d <- d[!(d$ID %in% gone & d$Week == 12), ]
  d$Week_f <- factor(d$Week)
  f <- suppressMessages(lmer(y ~ Group * Week_f + (1 | ID), data = d))
  coef(summary(f))["GroupProtein:Week_f12", "Pr(>|t|)"]
}

set.seed(42)
p <- replicate(pw_nsim, sim_trial(pw_n, pw_delta, sd_res = pw_sdres, drop = pw_drop))
pow <- mean(p < 0.05)
cat(sprintf("Power = %.2f  (Monte Carlo SE %.3f, %d simulated trials)\n",
            pow, sqrt(pow * (1 - pow) / pw_nsim), pw_nsim))
```

::: {.small-note}
Set the difference to 0 to check the Type I error: it should be close to 0.05. Then halve the residual SD and see how much power improves. Reducing day-to-day measurement noise (standardized scan conditions) is often cheaper than recruiting more people.
:::

## Exercises

### Q1 — Nested, averaged and wrong

```{webr}
#| exercise: l5q1
f_nest  <- lmer(VL_CSA_cm2 ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID/______), data = img)
f_avg   <- lmer(VL_CSA_cm2 ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID), data = csa)
f_wrong <- lmer(VL_CSA_cm2 ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID), data = img)

sapply(list(nested = f_nest, averaged = f_avg, wrong = f_wrong), function(f)
  coef(summary(f))["GroupProtein:Week_f12", c("Estimate", "Std. Error", "df")])
```

::: {.solution exercise="l5q1"}
Nest visits in participants: `(1 | ID/Week_f)`. Nested and averaged both give 0.990 (SE 0.282, df ≈ 71). The wrong model gives 0.994 with SE 0.159 and df ≈ 300: about 44% too small, because it treats day-to-day variation as if it were averaged over 3 independent visits.
:::

### Q2 — Where does the noise come from?

```{webr}
#| exercise: l5q2
f_nest <- lmer(VL_CSA_cm2 ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID/Week_f), data = img)
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(f_nest)); vc
s2_visit <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Week_f:ID"]
s2_image <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]
# SD of a visit mean with k images:
sapply(c(1, 3, 6), function(k) sqrt(s2_visit + s2_image / ______))
```

::: {.solution exercise="l5q2"}
Divide by `k`. Participant SD ≈ 2.94, visit SD ≈ 0.58, image SD ≈ 0.35 cm². A visit mean has SD ≈ 0.67 with 1 image, 0.61 with 3 and 0.60 with 6. More images barely help because day-to-day variance dominates. A second baseline visit, or tighter pre-scan standardization, is the better investment.
:::

### Q3 — Secondary outcomes and multiplicity

```{webr}
#| exercise: l5q3
diff12 <- function(f) {
  contrast(emmeans(f, ~ Group * Week_f),
           interaction = c("revpairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl"), ref = 1) |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |> tail(1)
}
f_lm <- lmer(Leg_Lean_Mass_kg ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID), data = sess)
f_rm <- lmer(log(Leg_Press_1RM_kg) ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID), data = sess)
lm12 <- diff12(f_lm); rm12 <- diff12(f_rm)
lm12; exp(rm12[, c("estimate", "lower.CL", "upper.CL")])
p.adjust(c(lean = lm12$p.value, strength = rm12$p.value), method = "______")
```

::: {.solution exercise="l5q3"}
`method = "holm"`. Lean mass +0.16 kg (0.03 to 0.29), p ≈ 0.016 (Holm 0.032); 1RM ratio 1.026 (0.968 to 1.087), p ≈ 0.38. A fixed sequence CSA → lean mass → 1RM gives the same conclusions: Protein increased muscle size by two measures, with no detectable effect on strength.
:::

### Q4 — Results figure

```{webr}
#| exercise: l5q4
#| fig-height: 4.5
fit <- lmer(VL_CSA_cm2 ~ Group * Week_f + Sex + (1 | ID), data = csa)
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans(fit, ~ Group * Week_f)) |>
  mutate(Week = as.numeric(as.character(Week_f)))
pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = csa, aes(Week, VL_CSA_cm2, group = ID, colour = Group), alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = emm_df, aes(Week, emmean, colour = Group), linewidth = 1, position = pd) +
  geom_pointrange(data = emm_df, aes(Week, emmean, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL,
                                     colour = Group), position = pd) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 6, 12)) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "VL CSA (cm²)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_classic()
```

::: {.hint exercise="l5q4"}
Run it as is, then try adding a second panel of **change from baseline** by arm, where the treatment effect is actually visible.
:::
